title: Monitoring training status with HR measures: do all roads lead to Rome?
population: Athletes (review of resting, exercise and recovery HR measures)
findings: Argues most contradictory findings in the literature relate to methodological inconsistencies or misinterpretation, not to limitations of HR measures.

Measures from 5-min (almost daily) resting recordings (beat-to-beat indices reflecting parasympathetic activity) and submaximal exercise HR (30- to 60-s average) are likely the most useful monitoring tools.
Individual-level interpretation should consider measurement error and the smallest important change, plus training context (phase, load, intensity distribution).
HR measures cannot inform on all aspects of wellness, fatigue and performance; combine with training logs, psychometric questionnaires and a countermovement jump.
limitations: Narrative expert review, no pooled effects and no quantitative thresholds in the abstract.
implications: Implement HRV/HR flags relative to the athlete's own smallest important change, not population cut-offs.
Prefer a standardised short recording or nightly average; mark missing or noisy days unknown rather than interpolating (engineering convention).
Interpret flags in the context of training phase.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, Front Physiol, first author Buchheit, 2014. Findings match Europe PMC abstract (PMID 24578692). Narrative review, level D.
